params.name: group_states
params.description: Comma-separated list of group states to filter monitors by (alert, ignored, no data, ok, skipped, unknown, warn)

params.name: name
params.description: Filter monitors by name substring match

params.name: tags
params.description: Comma-separated list of tags to filter monitors by

params.name: monitor_tags
params.description: Comma-separated list of monitor-specific tags to filter by

params.name: with_downtimes
params.description: When true, includes downtime information in the response

params.name: id_offset
params.description: Monitor ID to start paginating from (for cursor-based pagination)

params.name: page
params.description: The page number to retrieve (zero-indexed, for offset-based pagination)

params.name: page_size
params.description: The number of monitors to return per page (default 100, max 1000)

items.docs: Returns a paginated list of monitors for your Datadog organization. Results can be filtered by monitor type, group states, name tags, monitor tags, creator, and ID. Supports sorting by name, status, and type. Use this endpoint to audit your monitoring configuration or build monitoring dashboards.

Creates a new monitor with the specified configuration. The monitor type determines which query language and threshold options are available. Monitors can alert on metric thresholds, anomalies, log patterns, APM traces, synthetic test results, and more. Upon creation, Datadog begins evaluating the monitor against the defined query and will send notifications when alert conditions are met.

params.name: monitor_id
params.description: The unique numeric ID of the monitor to operate on

params.name: group_states
params.description: Comma-separated group states to include in the response (alert, ignored, no data, ok, skipped, unknown, warn)

params.name: with_downtimes
params.description: When true, includes active downtime information in the response

items.docs: Returns the configuration and current status of a specific monitor identified by its ID. Includes the monitor query, notification settings, alert thresholds, and current group statuses. Optionally includes downtime and creator information.

params.name: monitor_id
params.description: The unique numeric ID of the monitor to operate on

items.docs: Updates the configuration of an existing monitor identified by its ID. The request body replaces the entire monitor configuration, so include all desired fields in the update. Changes to the query or thresholds take effect immediately. Updating notification channels or message templates applies to future alerts.

params.name: monitor_id
params.description: The unique numeric ID of the monitor to operate on

params.name: force
params.description: When true, forcefully deletes the monitor even if it is referenced by SLOs or composite monitors

items.docs: Permanently deletes the monitor with the specified ID. Deletion cannot be undone. Active alerts and notifications for the monitor are immediately cancelled. Any associated SLOs referencing this monitor must be updated before the monitor can be deleted.

params.name: monitor_id
params.description: The unique numeric ID of the monitor to operate on

items.docs: Mutes the specified monitor to suppress alert notifications for all groups or specific scopes. Optionally specify an end time after which the monitor automatically unmutes. While muted, the monitor continues to evaluate the query but does not send alert notifications. Useful for planned maintenance or known issues.

params.name: monitor_id
params.description: The unique numeric ID of the monitor to operate on

items.docs: Unmutes a previously muted monitor to resume alert notifications. Optionally specify a scope to unmute only specific groups. If no scope is specified, the monitor is unmuted globally across all groups. Notifications resume immediately for any groups that are in an alert or warning state.

Validates a monitor configuration without creating it. Returns validation errors if the monitor query, type, or options are invalid. Use this endpoint to test monitor configurations programmatically before deploying them to production. Validation checks syntax, query correctness, and compatibility of monitor type with specified options.
